title: Remembered vs recorded

rows.remembered: The dedup / cross-language experiments were the simplifying win.
rows.recorded: Dedup itself lost 14.43 pts and was killed; the simplification was the flat gallery + a 1,538-param language head (67.66 → 77.61% print@1). The negative result was the win.
The bar first appears 09-11 19:37 PDT (evening plan); 09-13 is a restatement.
Small-sample high. The pooled 87-lot run gives 71.3% overall, 65.2% on non-locked lots.

rows.remembered: Overlapping commit dates read as concurrent work — arc B rebuilt as parallel spines.
rows.recorded: Founder corrected it: not concurrent. Four sequential acts, each begun for a stated reason.
rows.label: the record can be over-read too

rows.remembered: Absent from the mined transcript corpus → treated as unsourced, dropped.
rows.recorded: Founder testimony stands; the message simply lived outside the mined corpus (a second account).
rows.label: absence from the corpus ≠ unsourced

rows.instance: E79: one crop vs the 5-crop vote
rows.remembered: A 09-13 replay read as undoing the single-crop win (25 vs 24).
rows.recorded: Founder: the single crop won, and E79b stands: 31 vs 26 of 41 at 337 vs 1,893 ms; ledger verdict ‘drop the vote hack’. The 09-13 replay compared two single crops (b00 vs b17), never the vote.
rows.label: a ‘replication’ that tested different arms

caption: Three rows where the record corrects memory. Three counter-examples, marked apart, where the record was over-read and the person who was there corrected it. Keep both records, and check in both directions.
